text:
simon: heads-up, seeing p99 jump ~3x for ap-southeast yesterday evening. dashboard: https://redwood/d/serving/p99?var=region=ap-southeast :eyes:

maria: ah, I pushed a routing policy change yday to be more aggressive with cross-region fallbacks (fallback_rate_threshold 5% -> 2.5%) to reduce cost. did we run rehearsals?

kevin: deploy-bot shows that change rolled with 2026-11-02 22:14 UTC. also there was a kernel tweak in commit 9f2b that switched small-batch kernel selection to quantized fast-path.

anya: profiler snapshots (flame) show long tail in kernel_qv_fast for microbatch sizes 8-16. L3 miss rate up, and KV cache entries evicted earlier -> more backend fetches cross-region.

simon: quick query from logs: p95=120ms p99=1.8s, baseline was p95=90ms p99=600ms. majority of p99 samples include a remote_fetch marker.

alex: can we temporarily raise fallback threshold or pin routing to local-only? we need quick mitigation for SLO.

maria: I can rollback the routing change in 5m, or set region_policy=prefer_local for ap-southeast. which is faster?

kevin: rollback is ~2-3 minutes but risks extra churn. setting prefer_local override is a config flip, 30s. recommend override + disable kernel fast-path for small batches.

simon: how to disable kernel? any hot flag?

kevin: yes: at infra CLI:
```
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --kernel smallbatch_quant_fast=false --selector region=ap-southeast
```

anya: also cap microbatch to 4 for that region to avoid cache pressure:
```
redwoodctl runtime set-config --microbatch.max=4 --selector region=ap-southeast
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-override-ap-sea (maria) by maria@redwood — ETA 35s

maria: override applied. monitor p99. :thumbsup:

simon: initial 2m after override: p95=110ms p99=760ms — improving. :relieved:

anya: profiling shows kernel qv fast-path disabled; L3 miss-rate back to baseline, KV hit-rate back up ~12% -> remote fetches down.

alex: nice. plan: revert kernel change and re-run perf tests for microbatch sizes, update routing thresholds, add alert for KV-eviction amplification. who's owning follow-up?

maria: I'll own routing threshold change + alert. kevin/anya to run a focused perf sweep and write up a short postmortem.

kevin: will run sweep tomorrow and attach traces. initial suspicion: fast-path chosen heuristics didn't consider KV cache working set size -> causes eviction amplification under certain seq_len distributions.

simon: thanks all. adding notes to incident board. /cc @people-ops
